column1: # tests/oracle/sets.tsv — the option sets tools/oracle runs over every
# class v1: aspen must agree with `tree -n` byte for byte (stdout, stderr
# with the program name normalised, exit status; -o FILE's file too).
# class v2: aspen refuses the option by name, exit 2; tree's answer is
# measured and printed (status, bytes, lines). Since ap01 the v2 sets are
# --acl and --selinux alone (extended attributes, which wolf cannot read).
# Arguments are shell words (no globbing); %O is an output file per side.
# A --fromfile/--fromtabfile set runs over the fixture's input files
# instead of the directory roots (tools/oracle); a fourth column, when
# present, names a set's own roots: --filelimit with --du over roots that
# do not themselves trip the limit (SR-2.12: aspen's over-limit --du root
# is one directory where tree's is a file, which deviations.sh asserts). No set pairs -l with a
# for a visited link there in the host's directory order (DEVIATION D7,
# which deviations.sh asserts on aspen's sorted answer).
